title: Freya and the Contact
premise: Ansel Dravenmoor, a disgraced intelligence analyst living under a false name in a Baltic port town, receives calls on a burner phone from his dead mentor, Mara Voss, who feeds him fragments of a buried operation called CONTACT—a program that manufactures the very identities men like Ansel hide behind. Pursued by an assassin known only as the Cartographer and stonewalled by three governments that all deny CONTACT exists, Ansel must decide whether loyalty to the people who made him matters more than the truth of what they did. The trail ends in a decommissioned listening station where Ansel learns he was CONTACT's first product: his entire past, including his betrayal of Mara, was authored. In the end, Ansel broadcasts the archive publicly, sacrifices his false identity, and walks into custody as himself—finally belonging to no one but the truth.
about_author: Xanthe Okonkwo is a former maritime logistics analyst who spent a decade moving between port cities before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose paperwork is more real than they are.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Living quietly as a freight auditor in Gdańsk, Ansel rehearses his escape routes nightly, a habit from three burned careers. A routine audit turns up shipping manifests that shouldn't exist—cargoes that were never on any ship. Emotional beat: the itch of paranoia returning, the comfort of routine cracking.

chapters.title: Number You Do Not Know
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A burner phone appears in his mailbox, wrapped in oilcloth. When it rings, the voice is Mara Voss's—the mentor who died in a Vienna safehouse two years ago. She says one word: 'CONTACT.' Emotional beat: grief weaponized into dread; he can't hang up.

chapters.title: Three Names, One Man
chapters.summary: Mara's POV (flashback interwoven). Two years earlier, Mara discovered a cross-government program laundering analysts' identities and tried to report it. Her final night in Vienna replays with new meaning. Emotional beat: her fear curdling into resolve, and her decision to trust Ansel.

chapters.title: The Auditor's Alibi
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. He tests whether the call was a trap by feeding a false detail to his only local contact, a harbor clerk named Ieva. Within hours, someone asks Ieva about the false detail. Emotional beat: cold confirmation—he's already being hunted.

chapters.title: Cartography of Violence
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. The Cartographer, a methodical killer who maps targets' lives before touching them, receives Ansel's file and notes an anomaly: the file contradicts itself. Emotional beat: professional curiosity, the first hairline crack in his certainty.

chapters.title: Vienna, Rearranged
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel flies to Vienna using a third identity and breaks into the gutted safehouse where Mara died. Behind a radiator plate he finds her dead-drop notebook—half codes, half accusations against three agencies. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past has been physically rearranged to lie.

chapters.title: What Ieva Knew
chapters.summary: Ieva's POV. Back home, Ieva realizes the man she liked is someone else entirely, and that strangers have photographed her daughter's school. She must choose between warning him and protecting her family. Emotional beat: the cost of proximity to a hidden man.

chapters.title: The Denial Protocol
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel approaches a former handler in Berlin, who denies CONTACT exists while sweating through his shirt—and slips him a keycard instead of calling security. Emotional beat: betrayal wearing the mask of kindness; loyalty and truth pulling apart.

chapters.title: Intercepted
chapters.summary: Cartographer's POV. The Cartographer intercepts the Berlin meeting's surveillance and realizes his own agency is editing reality—his kill order predates the 'crime.' Emotional beat: a craftsman discovering his blueprint is forged.

chapters.title: The Voice on the Line
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Mara calls again and admits she isn't sure she's alive: the voice may be synthesized from her own recordings, which means either she's captive or the program can resurrect the dead as instruments. Emotional beat: longing and horror fused; he wants it to be her.

chapters.title: Harbor Lights
chapters.summary: Ieva's POV. Ieva passes Ansel a warning and, despite herself, helps him reach a container bound for Riga. The Cartographer lets them go—following is better than flushing. Emotional beat: reluctant solidarity; two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Riga Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Following Mara's notebook, Ansel retrieves a drive hidden in a church organ loft: CONTACT's personnel index, including his own original name—one he doesn't recognize. Emotional beat: identity dissolving; the self he defended may be fiction.

chapters.title: The First Product
chapters.summary: Mara's POV (flashback). Mara decodes CONTACT's founding documents years ago: the program authors analysts wholesale, memories coached, pasts printed. Ansel was its pilot subject. Emotional beat: her horror at loving a man built like a document.

chapters.title: Chorus of Denials
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel plays the evidence to contacts in three capitals; each government disavows CONTACT within hours of the other two, in identical language. Someone is orchestrating the silence. Emotional beat: claustrophobia—the walls are coordinated.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Map
chapters.summary: Cartographer's POV. Mapping Ansel's life, the Cartographer finds the same anomaly in his own history: gaps, contradictions, a childhood he can't verify. He stops hunting and starts asking. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing he is also quarry.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel and the defected Cartographer compare files and do the math: every witness to CONTACT is a CONTACT creation—including possibly Mara. The burner phone rings; this time it gives coordinates. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance; trust as a calculated risk.

chapters.title: The Listening Station
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The coordinates lead to a decommissioned Baltic listening station. Inside: servers, a recording studio, and a woman who looks exactly like Mara—or a perfect reconstruction. She claims to be the real one, kept alive because CONTACT needed her voice. Emotional beat: hope arriving dressed as a trap.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Audited
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Present-day Mara explains the endgame: CONTACT's directors plan to burn the archive and everyone in it, then rebuild the program elsewhere. She stayed inside to keep the archive intact—for Ansel to carry out. Emotional beat: love expressed as operational sacrifice.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. CONTACT's cleanup teams converge on the station; the Cartographer holds the causeway alone, buying minutes with everything he's learned about being underestimated. Emotional beat: defiant last stand; a made man choosing his own ending.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. With the station burning and Mara covering the retreat, Ansel uploads the full CONTACT archive to open servers worldwide before the servers die. The truth escapes; the lie machine does not. Emotional beat: catharsis—the moment hiding becomes impossible and freedom begins.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara, wounded, refuses extraction and stays with the archive's physical master, telling Ansel some truths need a keeper, not a broadcast. They part on the water's edge. Emotional beat: grief accepted rather than denied; love without possession.

chapters.title: Ansel Dravenmoor
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel surrenders voluntarily, giving investigators his real name—the one from the drive—and testifies for months. Released, he unpacks the go-bag at last and keeps one burner phone, silent, charged. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; belonging found not in a name, but in standing behind one.
